newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran complains U.S. forces violated its territory.
newsitem.headline: Iran complains U.S. forces violated its territory.

text.p: Iran has complained to the United Nations over alleged violations of its territory by U.S. forces in the Gulf, the official news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.
In a letter to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Monday, Iran called "for an end to illegal measures by the U.S. warships in the regional waters of the Islamic republic of Iran."

The letter cited two alleged incidents including one when a U.S. warship opened fire on two Iranian boats 7.2 km (4.5 miles) from the Soroush oil platform in the Gulf. It did not say when the incident took place.

It said the other incident happened on February 26 when a U.S. helicopter "flew over an Iranian boat navigating 128 km (80 miles) from the Iranian port of Ganaveh. The Iranian boat, filled with water and in danger of sinking, was forced to change course towards the Iranian mainland."
IRNA said Iran had on July 3 protested the two incidents to the U.S. State Department through Iran's interest section at the Pakistani embassy in Washington.
Washington has in the past denied similar Iranian charges.
The United States, which has vowed to protect its Gulf Arab allies from any potential security threats from Iran and Iraq, has a strong naval and air presence in the Gulf.
Iran has repeatedly condemned the U.S. military presence in the region, where U.S.-led forces enforce U.N. sanctions against Iraq.
